summary: Track 21 (Continuous/Streaming Audit Mode) research complete. Recommends a two-layer design: Layer 1 keeps the existing one-shot weekly audit (Fairlearn+AIF360, χ² α=0.05, bootstrap B≥1000, n≥30 guard) completely unchanged; Layer 2 adds a CUSUM control chart over the resulting per-window Core-Four point estimates to detect sustained drift across batches. Rejected per-record sequential testing (violates n≥30, provably inflates Type-I error under naive continuous monitoring) and FairCanary's QDD metric (would add a 5th, non-Core-Four metric, breaking the M1 lock). Proposes an additive-only `DriftObservation` dataclass (run_id, window bounds, CUSUM stats, watch/alarm flags) that references MetricResult by value without modifying it. Alerting is two-tier: Watch (CUSUM threshold alone, logged) vs Alarm (CUSUM threshold AND a fresh within-window χ² significance — dual-gate to avoid single-batch false alarms). Flags formal Lan-DeMets alpha-spending as an optional, separately-scoped follow-on if a provable cross-batch Type-I bound is ever required. Differentiates from Aequitas/Fairlearn/AIF360 (no temporal support at all) and from FairCanary (temporal support exists but trades away labeled, statistically-audited metrics for an unsupervised distributional one). Draft FR-XXX spec section included, not applied to any file. Research-only — no code/repo edits, no sync.ps1. Full markdown at research/results/21_streaming_audit_mode.md (also delivered to user as a file this session).
